'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**[[Siege of Djibo]]
***At least 40 civilians are killed and 42 more injured after [[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]] tried to take control of the town of [[Djibo]], [[Burkina Faso]]. [https://apnews.com/article/burkina-faso-al-qaida-linked-attack-un-f5a96076ac84148259e48a82ca6d7484 (AP)]
*[[2023 Freetown attacks]]
**[[Sierra Leone]] declares a national [[curfew]] following an attack by [[militant]]s on [[barracks]] in [[Freetown]]. The militants later [[prison escape|break into]] [[Freetown Central Prison]], setting some inmates free. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/sierra-leone-security-forces-repelled-attack-barracks-govt-statement-2023-11-26/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis]]
***[[2023 Israel–Hamas ceasefire]]
****[[Hamas]] releases three [[Thai people|Thai]] [[migrant worker]]s and 14 [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[hostage]]s, while [[Israel]] releases 39 [[Palestinian prisoners]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/14-israelis-9-of-them-children-freed-by-hamas-on-3rd-day-of-hostages-for-truce-deal/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Red Sea crisis]], [[Attacks on U.S. bases in Iraq, Jordan, and Syria (2023–present)]]
***[[Houthi movement|Houthi forces]] fire two [[ballistic missile]]s at the [[USS Mason (DDG-87)|USS ''Mason'']], with both missiles landing short of the ship in the [[Gulf of Aden]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/us-navy-responds-distress-call-israeli-owned-tanker-seized-coast-yemen (Fox News)]
***Armed assailants seize and later release a [[tanker (ship)|tanker]] linked to Israeli [[billionaire]] [[Eyal Ofer]], with 22 crew members on board, off the coast of [[Yemen]]. The [[United States Navy]] captures the attackers. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-hamas-war-yemen-ship-attack-526842504dc9f6bb7ca6e1d5104f77a3 (AP)]
**Eight [[Palestinians]] are killed and at least six others are injured in [[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli]] raids in the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/26/israeli-forces-carry-out-deadly-raids-in-the-west-bank-amid-gaza-truce (Al Jazeera)]
**The [[Palestine Red Crescent Society]] says that a [[Palestinian farmer]] was killed and another was injured when they were targeted by Israeli forces in the [[Maghazi (camp)|Maghazi refugee camp]] in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/palestinian-farmer-killed-by-israeli-forces-gaza-refugee-camp-palestinian-red-2023-11-26/ (Reuters)]
**Hamas confirms the deaths of several senior commanders including [[Ahmed Ghandour (militant)|Ahmed Ghandour]], the commander of its [[Northern Gaza]] [[brigade]], and Ayman Siam, the head of its rocket firing array. The Israel Defense Forces had previously said it had targeted Ghandour and Siam, but did not confirm that they had been killed. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/hamas-confirms-senior-commanders-killed-in-earlier-gaza-fighting/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] becomes the first Israeli [[head of government]] to enter the Gaza Strip in two decades, after visiting Israel Defense Forces troops stationed there. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-775242 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[2023 Booker Prize]]
**[[Irish literature|Irish writer]] [[Paul Lynch (writer)|Paul Lynch]] wins the [[Booker Prize]] for his novel ''[[Prophet Song]]''. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20231126-irish-author-paul-lynch-wins-2023-booker-prize (AFP via RFI)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*The [[cargo ship]] ''Raptor'' sinks off the [[Greek island]] of [[Lesbos]] with 14 crew members on board. The [[Hellenic Coast Guard|coast guard]] rescues one person and recovers the body of one of the other crew members. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231126-search-underway-for-13-missing-after-ship-sinks-off-greek-island (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Malaysia relations]], [[India–Malaysia relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Malaysian Prime Minister]] [[Anwar Ibrahim]] announces at a [[People's Justice Party (Malaysia)|People's Justice Party]] congress that citizens of [[China]] and [[India]] will have [[visa-free travel]] from December 1, allowing stays of up to 30 days in a bid to boost [[tourism in Malaysia|tourism]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/malaysia-allow-visa-free-entry-china-india-citizens-dec-1-pm-2023-11-27/ (Reuters)]
*[[Germany–Mali relations]]
**[[Germans|German]] [[Catholic priest]] [[Hans-Joachim Lohre]], who disappeared in [[Bamako]], [[Mali]], in November 2022 and was presumed [[Kidnapping|kidnapped]], is released and returns to [[Germany]]. [https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/1132834-german-priest-abducted-in-mali-in-2022-freed (AFP via ''The News'')]
*[[Guyana–Venezuela relations]]
**[[President of Guyana|Guyanese President]] [[Irfaan Ali]] visits the region of [[Guayana Esequiba]] and hoists the [[Guyanese flag]], amid heightening tensions with [[Venezuela]] over the territory. Venezuela calls the action a "provocation". [https://eleconomista.com.ar/internacional/sube-tension-venezuela-guyana-n68741 (''El Economista'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Corruption in Kuwait]]
**[[Kuwait]]'s highest court [[sentence (law)|sentences]] former [[Ministry of Defense (Kuwait)|defense]] and [[Ministry of Interior (Kuwait)|interior minister]] [[Khaled Al Jarrah Al Sabah]] to seven years in prison for mishandling military funds while former [[Prime Minister of Kuwait|Prime Minister]] [[Jaber Al-Mubarak Al-Hamad Al-Sabah]], who faced similar [[criminal charge|charges]], is only ordered by the court to return the funds that he mismanaged. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2023/11/26/Kuwait-s-top-court-sentences-former-defense-minister-to-seven-years-in-prison (Reuters via Al Arabiya)]
*[[Violent incidents in reaction to the 2023 Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Anti-Palestinianism during the 2023 Israel–Hamas war]]
***[[2023 shooting of Palestinian students in Burlington, Vermont]]
****Three students of Palestinian ethnicity are shot and injured by an unknown attacker in [[Burlington, Vermont|Burlington]], [[Vermont]], [[United States]], in what police are investigating as a possible hate crime. [https://time.com/6339781/three-palestinian-students-shot-injured-vermont/ (''Time'')]
*Three people are killed and two others are critically injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a residence in [[Winnipeg]], [[Manitoba]], [[Canada]]. [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2023/11/26/Shooting-in-Winnipeg-leaves-three-people-dead-two-in-critical-condition/2541701049200/ (UPI)]

'''Sports'''

**[[2023 Davis Cup]]
***In [[tennis]], [[Italy Davis Cup team|Italy]] wins its first [[Davis Cup]] title since [[1976 Davis Cup|1976]] after defeating [[Australia Davis Cup team|Australia]] 2–0 in the [[2023 Davis Cup Finals|finals]].
